newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fraud probe into manager at bankrupt Traub.
newsitem.headline: Fraud probe into manager at bankrupt Traub.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Thursday they were investigating a senior manager at bankrupt machine tool-maker Traub AG on suspicions of fraud.
A spokesman for the Stuttgart prosecutors' office said the investigation was a follow-up to an official complaint, but declined to give further details.

It was unclear whether the probe was connected to the collapse of Traub, which opened bankruptcy proceedings in court earlier this week after failing to reach agreement with creditors to restructure its multi-million-mark debts.
Traub first went into serious crisis last October when it declared itself insolvent amid debts of some 350 million marks -- becoming the latest in a series of mid-sized German firms to go under.

However on Thursday Traub issued a statement to say its administrator would start discussing a takeover offer by the Esslingen-based firm Index-Werke GmbH -- like Traub, a leading manufactuer of motorised lathes -- over the next few days.
Traub said it hoped to agree a firm offer shortly so that a takeover deal could go ahead in early March.
A rival proposal by machine-manufacturer Gildemeister AG, which would have saved more jobs at Traub's main plant in Reichenbach, was withdrawn on Thursday after having been rejected by the banks.
Traub currently has some 750 workers left, of which Index, which has some 1,550 staff, is expected to keep 450.
Index last year increased its turnover by 10 percent to 440 million marks.
In the red for years, Traub had sales of 223.9 million marks but suffered a loss of 16.4 million marks in the first six months of 1996
